memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's target argument must be a deploy-tree root (a repo root holding both a deployed .claude/ tree and, for source-store work, agent-system/extensions simultaneously) -- never an extension's own source_dir subdirectory, which has no .claude/ and makes gate 0 exit before gate selection. For a source-store-adjacent check, resolve the repo root as the directory containing .claude-extensions.json and pass that as TARGET, e.g. `bash <repo_root>/.claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4 <repo_root>`.

A repo-wide lint/sweep/grep criterion in a verification step should be phrased as a baseline delta or scoped to the files a phase touches, never as an absolute zero -- a baseline is a moving quantity and a criterion hard-coding one is wrong the moment it moves in either direction. A gate failing only on pre-existing findings outside the task's file scope is a recorded PASS, not a blocker, and must never be cleared by editing out-of-scope files.

When a shared source-store repository's working tree already carries pre-existing, uncommitted foreign changes from another in-flight session before a task even begins, a deploy-time verification gate (e.g. deploy-headless.sh's inline RESULT check) can fail for reasons entirely attributable to that foreign content. The correct response is to diff-attribute each failing finding to the specific foreign file causing it (never assume; measure), never hand-patch the foreign file, and close the phase [PARTIAL] per the plan's own rollback instruction rather than forcing green.
